title: Design System: AI Product Intelligence Advisor

world.name: Daylight Glass (light Liquid Glass)

display.purpose: SKU code atop the focus panel; Latin-only, so 1.2 is allowed.

headline.purpose: Dashboard title; balanced wrap, max 36ch; 1.25 under html[lang=en]; 20px below 760px.

key-figure.purpose: Values in the four key-fact tiles of the focus panel.

rank.purpose: Card rank numeral (ties add a small '='); chat rows use 16px.

title.purpose: The action name beside the status chip in the focus panel.

card-title.purpose: SKU code on a product card.

body.purpose: Default text, inputs and buttons (buttons at 600).

label.purpose: Badges, small chips, freshness heading, key-fact labels (at 400).

caption.purpose: Nav sub-labels, card fact labels, TV caption.

fonts.family: System UI (-apple-system, SF Pro Text, Segoe UI, Roboto)

numerals.scope: Figures, ranks, counts and key facts (.num, .fig, .key-facts dd, .rank, .count).

materials.name: glass
materials.value: background: var(--glass-bg); backdrop-filter: blur(28px) saturate(175%); border: 1px solid var(--glass-stroke); border-radius: 22px; box-shadow: var(--glass-shadow)
materials.purpose: Control layer only: sidebar, toolbar, chat composer, decision bar.

materials.name: glass-fallback-no-backdrop
materials.value: @supports not ((backdrop-filter: blur(1px)) or (-webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(1px))) { .glass { background: rgba(250, 251, 253, 0.97); } }
materials.purpose: Near-opaque glass where backdrop-filter is unsupported.

materials.name: glass-fallback-reduced-transparency
materials.purpose: Solid control layer for users who reduce transparency.

materials.name: surface
materials.purpose: All content: cards, focus panel, answer bubbles, empty state.

materials.name: popover
materials.purpose: Demo controls and decision rationale; always solid (no glass on glass).

wallpaper.purpose: One flat daylight ground for page, gutters and scroll-edge fades; no gradient light fields.

shadows.name: glass-shadow
shadows.purpose: Specular top edge, soft bottom edge, ambient drop and contact shadow of glass.

shadows.name: card-hover
shadows.purpose: Product card lifted on hover (with translateY(-2px)).

shadows.name: selected-ring
shadows.purpose: Selected product card; pressed decision button uses the bare 2px ring.

fades.name: toolbar-scroll-edge
fades.value: ::before, linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(238, 241, 246, 0.9) 50%, rgba(238, 241, 246, 0)), extends 16px past the bar
fades.purpose: Content fades before passing under the sticky toolbar.

fades.name: decision-dock-scroll-edge
fades.value: ::before, linear-gradient(to top, rgba(238, 241, 246, 0.94) 55%, rgba(238, 241, 246, 0)), 56px taller than the dock
fades.purpose: Content fades before passing under the floating decision bar.

focus.purpose: Global :focus-visible ring; search field shows a 2px accent box-shadow ring on focus-within.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: background-color/color on segments, tabs, filters, chips, answer rows, source lines, buttons.

motion.name: duration-lift
motion.purpose: Card transform and shadow on hover.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: 232px labelled glass sidebar with data freshness | fluid main; focus TV 300px.

breakpoints.name: icon-rail
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: sidebar collapses to a 76px icon rail, labels visually hidden, freshness hidden; focus TV 240px.

breakpoints.name: focus-stack
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: focus hero stacks, TV centred.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: sidebar becomes a fixed glass bottom tab bar; toolbar wraps; rail cards 160px; key facts 2 columns; dock and composer at bottom 84px; decision bar shows buttons only.

narrative.overview:
A calm, light workspace in Apple's Liquid Glass idiom. One flat, cool daylight ground (Wallpaper) sits behind everything: gutters, page and scroll-edge fades are the same colour, so no band or seam ever shows. Frosted glass carries only the controls and navigation (the sidebar, the toolbar, the chat composer and the floating decision bar). The content sits on solid white surfaces below that layer, so the product and its verdict lead and the evidence waits one click away. The world rejects two things. One is the dense ledger table of the superseded "Market Page" direction. The other is the dark KPI-tile dashboard full of invented numbers.

Two pages share one shell. **Chat & Advisor** (`/`) is a centred conversation. The fixed north-star question appears as a blue bubble. The answer is a white bubble holding one composed sentence, the ranking basis and ranked rows with a small TV thumbnail. A glass composer offers preset follow-up chips, and there is no free-text input because no LLM exists. **Product dashboard** (`/dashboard`) has a title and meta line, status filters with counts, a horizontal rail of product cards, a focus panel for the selected SKU, and a floating glass decision bar.

Thai is the primary language and English is switchable. The system UI typeface carries Latin, and self-hosted Noto Sans Thai carries Thai. Line-heights leave room for stacked Thai vowel and tone marks. All data is synthetic and says so on the page.
keyCharacteristics: Liquid Glass control layer floating over solid white content; never glass on glass.
Size-true synthetic TV illustrations: plain SVG geometry scaled from the real screen diagonal.
Progressive disclosure: verdict and four key facts first; rules, alternatives and evidence behind one-click tabs.
iOS status hues used only for status, always with the same icon on every surface.
Status counts are the only aggregate figures; there is no score and no KPI tile.
Redaction is always visible as a lock, never as a silent gap.

rules.name: The Control Layer Rule
rules.body: Glass is reserved for the sidebar, the toolbar, the chat composer and the decision bar. Every piece of content (cards, the focus panel, answer bubbles, popovers) sits on a solid surface.

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: A status hue means the same thing on every surface: chip, filter, callout, rule outcome, verdict tag and data state. Hues colour text and icons only. A tint appears only as the background of a status chip or a callout. Status colour never marks a region, a brand element or a provenance mark.

rules.name: The Blue Means Act Rule
rules.body: System Blue marks what is selected, what can be done next, and where a figure came from. It never encodes a status.

rules.name: The Thai Headroom Rule
rules.body: Anything that can carry Thai keeps a line-height of 1.4 or more. Only digit-only or Latin-only elements go tighter: the rank, the mark, the SKU code display, and the English headline.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every figure, rank, count and key fact uses `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`. Figures do not wrap.

rules.name: The One-Click Evidence Rule
rules.body: The first view shows the verdict and four key facts. Rules, alternatives and evidence sit one tab away, and they are never two clicks deep.

rules.name: The No Glass on Glass Rule
rules.body: Anything that opens from a glass bar (the demo popover, the decision popover) is a solid surface. Glass never stacks on glass.

rules.name: The Solid Fallback Rule
rules.body: Without `backdrop-filter` support, glass becomes near-opaque white (rgba(250, 251, 253, 0.97)). Under `prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce` it becomes solid #f6f7f9 with no blur. The control layer must stay legible with no frost at all.

rules.name: The No Refraction Rule
rules.body: There is no SVG displacement or refraction filter. The frost, the specular top edge and the inner stroke carry the material.

rules.name: The Size-True Rule
rules.body: A TV illustration's width always comes from its real screen size, so a 65″ set reads as larger than a 43″ set. It is decorative (`aria-hidden`) in cards and chat rows. It is labeled as synthetic, with a caption, on the focus panel. It must never look like a product photo.

rules.name: The Lock Rule
rules.body: Every redaction shows a lock: a redacted value is a lock plus "Redacted" (lock alone in compact cells), a withheld rank is a lock tile, a redacted rule outcome carries a lock, and the demo button shows a lock at internal clearance. Redaction is never an empty cell.

rules.name: The Counts-Only Rule
rules.body: Status counts (on the filters and in the chat breakdown) are the only aggregate figures on any page. Per-SKU key facts are shown, but there are no aggregate KPI tiles, no score, no "potential" label and no discount percentage.

dos: **Do** keep glass on the control layer only (the sidebar, toolbar, composer and decision bar), and keep every popover and piece of content solid.
**Do** ship both glass fallbacks: `@supports not (backdrop-filter)` and `prefers-reduced-transparency`.
**Do** use the four status hues with their fixed icons on every surface, with tints only behind chips and callouts.
**Do** show every status as a filter with its count, even when the count is 0, and show "Internal data only" on every answer.
**Do** show a lock wherever something is redacted.
**Do** scale TV illustrations from the real screen size, and label the large one as synthetic.
**Do** keep line-height at 1.4 or more on anything that can carry Thai.
**Do** keep motion to the shared ease (cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)): 180ms background changes, a 200ms card lift, a 120ms press. Remove all of it under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** keep Ink 3 as the lightest text colour.
donts: **Don't** put glass on glass, or glass behind content (cards, the focus panel, bubbles, tables).
**Don't** use SVG refraction or displacement filters.
**Don't** show aggregate KPI tiles, scores, success probabilities, "top/potential" badges, discount percentages or placeholder market signals. External sources read "not connected".
**Don't** use status hues for decoration, brand accents or provenance marks. Don't use System Blue to mean a status.
**Don't** add a free-text chat input or imply generated answers while no LLM exists.
**Don't** let a TV illustration look like a product photo, or carry a brand mark.
**Don't** hide insufficient, review or blocked SKUs behind a click, or let redacted data disappear without a lock.
